newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Danish truckers strike hits Singapore freighter.
newsitem.headline: Danish truckers strike hits Singapore freighter.

text.p: A Singapore Airlines Ltd freighter would leave Denmark on Wednesday carrying less than half of its capacity because of a truckers' strike, costing the airline a million Swedish crowns, an airline spokesman said.

Singapore Airlines' cargo manager for Scandinavia and Finland Jens Heide told Reuters that freight the airline normally trucked from Sweden and within Denmark was stopped because of the Danish truckers' strike.
"It means we will go half empty today...we only have a load factor of 40 percent and we were expecting 100 percent.
"We will lose approximately one million Swedish crowns because of the strike stopping traffic from Stockholm, Gothenburg, Malmo and all around Denmark," Heide said.
He said this was the first Singapore Airlines freight flight from Denmark seriously hit by the strike, now three days old.
Danish truckers were striking to protest government plans to cut drivers' overseas subsistence allowances, sealing off a land border with Germany and blocking most seaports.
"We had cargo but it was stopped at the border," Heide said.

Singapore Airlines flies a Boeing 747 frieghter, with a capacity of about 128 tonnes, from Copenhagen to Singapore via Delhi twice weekly on Wednesdays and Sundays. The carrier also flies passenger flights from the Danish capital.
Heide said the frieghter had been averaging a 100 percent load factor since September, the start of the peak season.
The airline may re-route its Sunday flight, possibly through Stockholm, Heide said.
"We will re-route our weekend freighter to touch down in Stockholm if the strike continues."
